title: Compatibility of the six operations
statement:
Fix the coefficient stages of [sk-def-sf-setting] and the six operations
$Lf^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,Rf^!,\otimes^L,\RHom$ of [sk-thm-sf-package], each typed
as there ([sk-thm-sf-package]). The structure isomorphisms that relate them
— the composition isomorphisms, the units and counits of the two
adjunctions, the exchange transformations, the projection transformation,
the proper identification $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$, the tensor–Hom and Verdier
exchanges and the orientation — are compatible with each other, on the
categories on which [sk-thm-sf-package] types each of them:

1. **(1)** *Composition.* The composition isomorphisms
$L(gf)^*\cong Lf^*Lg^*$ ([prop-sfb-module-left-derived-upper-star-comp]),
$R(gf)_*\cong Rg_*Rf_*$ (its mate under $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$),
$R(gf)_!\cong Rg_!Rf_!$ ([thm-sf-comp-composition]) and
$R(gf)^!\cong Rf^!Rg^!$ ([lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (2)-(3)) are associative and
unital, and each isomorphism for a right adjoint is the mate of the one for
its left adjoint, so that the units and counits of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ and
$Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ are compatible with composition. The functor $Rf_!$ is
independent of the compactification, with comparison isomorphisms satisfying
the cocycle condition and compatible with the composition law
([prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] at finite coefficients and [fix-lem-exchanges] (4) at the other stages).
1. **(2)** *Base change.* The exchange transformations
$\operatorname{Ex}_*$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ of [sk-def-sf-exchanges]
are natural in the square, the identity for the identity square and
compatible with horizontal and vertical pasting; $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is
compatible with the refinement comparisons and the composition law of (1)
([fix-lem-exchanges]), and for proper $f$ it is $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ under
$Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ ([sk-thm-sf-package] (4), [def-exchange-projection]). The inverse of its right-adjoint conjugate is the dual base
change isomorphism $Rf^!Rg_*\cong Rg'_*Rf'^!$, natural in the square and
compatible with pasting ([thm-sf-dual-base-change]), and for smooth $f$ the
exceptional base change $Lg'^*Rf^!\cong Rf'^!Lg^*$ of [sk-thm-sf-package] (5) is the exceptional-adjunction transpose of $\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}$ followed by the pulled-back counit, on the base-change domains of [sk-thm-sf-package] (5).
1. **(3)** *Tensor product.* The projection transformation
$\operatorname{PF}$ is natural, the identity for $f=\mathrm{id}$,
associative for composable $f,g$ with respect to the composition law of
(1), independent of the compactification, equal for proper $f$ to the
direct-image projection formula through $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$, and compatible
with base change through $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ and the monoidality of
$Lg^*$ ([prop-sf-pf-coherence]).
1. **(4)** *Internal Hom and duality.* The tensor–Hom exchange
$Rf_*\RHom_X(M,Rf^!N)\cong\RHom_Y(Rf_!M,N)$ of
[sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] is built from the adjunctions and the inverse of
$\operatorname{PF}$, and is natural in $M$ and $N$. With
$\mathbb D=\RHom(-,\omega)$ and biduality
([thm-sf-biduality-class]), the Verdier exchange
$\mathbb D_YRf_!\cong Rf_*\mathbb D_X$ ([sk-thm-sf-verdier-exchange])
is compatible with composition ([sk-thm-sf-package] (6)), and its mate is
the isomorphism $\mathbb D_XLf^*\cong Rf^!\mathbb D_Y$, natural in $f$
([cor-sf-duality-pullback]).
1. **(5)** *Orientation.* For smooth $f$ the purity isomorphism
$\gamma_f:Lf^*(-)(d)[2d]\cong Rf^!$ of [sk-def-sf-orientation] is
compatible with composition through the isomorphism
$R(gf)^!\cong Rf^!Rg^!$ of (1), and with base change through the
exceptional base change of (2) — along arbitrary $g$ at $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$,
along étale $g$ at the other stages ([sk-thm-sf-package] (5)).
1. **(6)** *Products.* The relative Künneth isomorphism of
[sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative] is compatible with symmetry, triple products,
base change and the projection formula.
1. **(7)** *Coefficients.* All of the maps above commute with finite
reduction and scalar extension, and at field coefficients they are
Weil-equivariant ([fix-prop-coherence]).

No compatibility of the Verdier exchange with base change along an arbitrary
$g$ is asserted, since $\mathbb D$ does not commute with $Lg^*$ in general.

proof.text: Use precisely the coefficient categories in [sk-thm-sf-package]: ordinary finite etale categories and witnessed pro-etale realizations, completed integral categories, raw rationalization, and common finite field stages. Its clauses (1), (2), (3), (4), (5), (6) and (8) supply the operations, adjunctions, invertible exchanges/projections and their stated domains. In particular the exceptional adjoints used below are constructible adjoints; no ambient exceptional-adjoint hypothesis is introduced. Thus the concrete package supplies the hypotheses of the six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] whenever a later cited formal theorem is stated for that datum. The datum axioms that those clauses do not display at every stage, namely the pentagon of (A4) for the completed, rational and common-stage composition laws and the coefficient compatibilities (A5), are the identity/composition coherence and the coefficient comparisons of [fix-prop-coherence] for the same operations of [def-fix-six-functor-datum].

source.place: Proof, initial sentence: fix the individually proved operations and their domains

proof.text:
At a finite coefficient stage the canonical derived module pullback comparison of [prop-sfb-module-left-derived-upper-star-comp] is induced by underived module pullback composition. In its factorized ringed-sheaf computation, [lem-sfb-module-mapmod-pullback-kflat] ensures that transport by the abelian inverse image takes a chosen K-flat module complex to a K-flat complex over the pulled-back ring; hence the subsequent derived scalar-extension factor uses that transported complex. This checks the resolution hypothesis in the module factorization, rather than treating abelian sheaf pullback as the whole module functor. The composition coherence statement of [fix-prop-coherence] gives associativity and units for the resulting comparisons at all stages. The adjunction normalization of [fix-prop-adjunctions](3) makes the direct-image comparison its conjugate, with
$$\eta_{gf}=(Rg_*\eta_f Lg^*)\eta_g,\qquad \varepsilon_{gf}=\varepsilon_f(Lf^*\varepsilon_g Rf_*).$$
The pasting and identity statements of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1),(2),(4) give the same coherence for direct images. At nonfinite stages use the actual completed and transported maps of the coherence theorem; no discrete non-torsion etale pullback is being substituted.

source.place: Canonical module pullback composition; its transported K-flat factor and the unit clause (1)

proof.text: At finite coefficients [thm-sf-comp-composition] supplies the associative, identity-normalized compact-support composition, independent of compactification, on bounded-below witnessed inputs. [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] supplies the refinement identities, transitivity and independence of a common refinement, hence the cocycle. For completed and field coefficients use the completed and transported composition forms explicitly included in [fix-lem-exchanges](2),(4), together with [sk-thm-sf-package](4). These are the same composition comparisons, not independently chosen isomorphisms. Clause (4) of [fix-lem-exchanges] intertwines refinement comparisons with composition. This proves the compact-support part of clause (1) at every stated stage, without applying the finite theorem directly to integral coefficients. Associativity and unitality of these completed and transported composition isomorphisms at the integral, rational and common-stage levels are the composition coherence of [fix-prop-coherence], whose operation datum has exactly this compact-support composition law.

source.place: Proof, clause (1): compact-support composition, cocycle and refinements

proof.text: Use the constructible exceptional adjunctions supplied by [sk-thm-sf-package](1), and take right-adjoint conjugates of the compact-support comparisons of step 3. The two associativity composites have equal conjugates by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2),(3); identity comparisons have identity mates by (4). Thus $R(gf)^!\cong Rf^!Rg^!$ is associative and unital. The same pasted-unit and pasted-counit normalization is part of [sk-thm-sf-package](1): explicitly the composite unit is $(Rf^!\nu_gRf_!)\nu_f$ and the composite counit is $\mu_g(Rg_!\mu_fRg^!)$. This proves the exceptional part of clause (1). No conditional ambient version of the mate lemma is needed.

source.place: Proof, clause (1): exceptional conjugates and composite adjunctions

proof.text: Apply [fix-lem-exchanges](1),(2),(4) to the canonical transformations: (1) gives object and square-comparison naturality; (2) gives identities and both pasting equations with the composition identifications inserted; (4) gives compactification/refinement and composition compatibility for $\operatorname{Ex}_!$. For proper $f$ choose $(j,p)=(\mathrm{id},f)$. In the defining compactification composite [def-exchange-projection] the open base-change arrow is then the identity, so the remaining arrow is exactly $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,f}$. At finite coefficients this identification is also [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence]; at higher stages the same computation uses the completed and transported formulas stated in [def-exchange-projection] and identified with the actual maps by [fix-lem-exchanges]. This proves the exchange and proper-coincidence assertions of clause (2).

source.place: Proof, clause (2): naturality, identity, pasting and proper coincidence

proof.text:
Apply [thm-sf-dual-base-change] to the datum verified in step 1. Under $Lg^*Rf_!\dashv Rf^!Rg_*$ and $Rf'_!Lg'^*\dashv Rg'_*Rf'^!$, it gives
$$Rf^!Rg_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg'_*Rf'^!$$
as the conjugate of $\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}$, equivalently the inverse conjugate of $\operatorname{Ex}_!$, with square naturality and both pasting compatibilities. This direction matters: the conjugate of $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ itself points the other way. The invertibility used here is the conjugacy of whole adjoint functors stated in that theorem, not a claim that every mate of an invertible square is invertible.

source.place: Proof, clause (2): dual base change and variance

proof.text:
For smooth $f$, [sk-thm-sf-package](5) identifies the smooth pullback exchange, at finite coefficients and along arbitrary $g$, with the transpose $T$ under $Rf'_!\dashv Rf'^!$ of
$$Rf'_!Lg'^*Rf^!K\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}}Lg^*Rf_!Rf^!K\xrightarrow{Lg^*\varepsilon_f}Lg^*K,$$
and says that under $\gamma_f,\gamma_{f'}$ it becomes the canonical isomorphism $b:Lg'^*Lf^*(-)(d)[2d]\cong Lf'^*Lg^*(-)(d)[2d]$, i.e. the trace is compatible with $\operatorname{Ex}_!$. At the other stages, for étale $g$ as in package (5), form the same $T$ from the constructible adjunctions of package (1) and the invertible $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ of package (2). There [sk-thm-purity-transport] makes $\gamma_f$ the isomorphism compatible with the counits, $\varepsilon_f\circ Rf_!(\gamma_f)=\mathrm{tr}_f$ for the normalized counit $\mathrm{tr}_f$ of $Rf_!\dashv Lf^*(-)(d)[2d]$, and compatible with base change; with package (5) this is $Lg^*\mathrm{tr}_f\circ\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}=\mathrm{tr}_{f'}\circ Rf'_!(b)$. Transpose under $Rf'_!\dashv Rf'^!$: by naturality of $\operatorname{Ex}_!$, $T\circ Lg'^*\gamma_f$ transposes to $Lg^*\varepsilon_f\circ Lg^*Rf_!\gamma_f\circ\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}=Lg^*\mathrm{tr}_f\circ\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}$, and $\gamma_{f'}\circ b$ to $\mathrm{tr}_{f'}\circ Rf'_!(b)$. Hence $T=\gamma_{f'}\circ b\circ(Lg'^*\gamma_f)^{-1}$ on every stated domain: $T$ is the purity composite through which package (5) states base change, and it is invertible because $\gamma_f,\gamma_{f'},b$ are. This square transpose is distinct from the whole-functor conjugate of step 6. No arbitrary-base-change orientation theorem is inferred at the nonfinite stages.

source.place: Proof, clauses (2) and (5): smooth exchange and its counit normalization

proof.text: For clause (3), apply [prop-sf-pf-coherence] to the concrete datum of step 1 and to the canonical projection transformation. Its statement supplies naturality, the identity normalization, the composition pentagon, compactification independence, proper coincidence, and the displayed base-change square using $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ and the monoidal pullback comparisons. The transformation here is the proper direct-image counit projection followed by the open tensor comparison of [def-exchange-projection]; it is the same map fixed in the package, so the coherence theorem applies to the specified map and not merely to an abstract isomorphism between its endpoints.

The tensor-Hom exchange of [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] is natural in both inputs. Its construction on test objects replaces $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!M\otimes^LL,N)$ by $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!(M\otimes^LLf^*L),N)$ using the inverse projection map, then applies exceptional adjunction, tensor-Hom transpose and ordinary adjunction. Thus the named exchange is built from the specified maps. [sk-thm-sf-package](6) identifies Verdier exchange with this tensor-Hom comparison at $N=\omega_Y$, followed by the dualizing-object identification $Rf^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$, and supplies its composition equation. [sk-thm-sf-verdier-exchange] supplies naturality on these concrete constructible domains. The dual pullback mate is constructed explicitly in the next step.

source.place: Proof, clause (4): construction, Verdier composition and dual pullback

proof.text:
Write $D_T=\mathbb D_T$ and $\mathcal C_T=D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$. By the biduality of [sk-thm-sf-package](6), $t_T(h)=D_T(h)\circ\delta_V$ gives a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_T(U,D_TV)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(V,D_TU)$: full faithfulness gives $\operatorname{Hom}_T(D_TD_TV,D_TU)$, and precomposition with $\delta_V$ gives the target. For $A\in\mathcal C_X$, $B\in\mathcal C_Y$, form
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_X(A,D_XLf^*B)&\xrightarrow{t_X}\operatorname{Hom}_X(Lf^*B,D_XA)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(B,Rf_*D_XA)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(B,D_YRf_!A)\\
&\xrightarrow{t_Y}\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!A,D_YB)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(A,Rf^!D_YB).
\end{aligned}$$
The second and last arrows are the ordinary and exceptional adjunctions of [sk-thm-sf-package](1); the middle arrow is postcomposition with the inverse Verdier exchange of [sk-thm-sf-verdier-exchange]. All objects lie in the displayed categories by package (6),(8). Denote the natural composite by $\Phi_{A,B}$. Put $U=D_XLf^*B$, $V=Rf^!D_YB$, and define $\chi_{f,B}=\Phi_{U,B}(1_U)$. Its inverse is $\Phi_{V,B}^{-1}(1_V)$: naturality in $A$ proves that the two composites are identities. Naturality in $B$ makes $\chi_f$ a transformation on $\mathcal C_Y^{op}$. This is precisely the adjoint transform of Verdier exchange, since its Hom action is the displayed chain. [cor-sf-duality-pullback] gives its identity and composition equations. Together with step 9 this proves clause (4), without any assertion that $D$ commutes with arbitrary base change.

source.place: Passing to adjoints, expanded as the natural Hom-adjunction chain using biduality

proof.text: For clause (5), use [sk-thm-sf-package](5). It states that the actual purity map is a natural isomorphism, that smooth composition adds the twists and shifts through the exceptional mate comparison, and that its base-change square uses the smooth exchange identified in step 7. The hypotheses are smooth separated finite type with pure relative dimension; composition is used for two such morphisms. The base change is arbitrary within the finite-type setting at $A_{E,n}$ and etale at the other stages, exactly as asserted. The component orientation of [sk-def-sf-orientation] is this same family, not an arbitrary trivialization of a dualizing object.

Apply [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative] with the same separated finite-type base $B$ and finite-Tor inputs. Its definition uses exactly the composition, inverse projection, inverse exchange, and symmetry maps already fixed. Its coherence clauses (i)-(iv) give respectively symmetry with Koszul signs, equality of the two triple-product composites, arbitrary base change through the three compact-support exchanges and monoidal pullback, and specialization to $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^{-1}$ when the second morphism is the identity. These four assertions prove clause (6) for the specified relative product, with the higher-coefficient meanings already included in that theorem. The separate projective-product lemma [lem-kun-bc-kunneth-compat] is not needed for this general assertion.

source.place: Proof, clause (6): the four relative product coherence equations

proof.text: Apply [fix-prop-coherence] to the proved comparison maps of the same operation system. It supplies coefficient coherence for ordinary operations, general finite-Tor internal Hom, integral Hom, finite coefficient-field extensions, exceptional comparisons and smooth orientation, and says that the field-stage maps are Weil-equivariant. Thus the primitive tensor, evaluation and adjunction maps used in steps 2-12 are intertwined by those comparisons. Applying a comparison functor to a composite applies it to each factor; an inverse is carried to the inverse whenever the compared arrows are isomorphisms. The same equations for units and counits intertwine their transposes. Consequently the displayed compositions, conjugates, projection/Hom exchanges and relative-product composites inherit the coefficient and Weil compatibilities, proving clause (7). Finite reduction is used at finite/integral stages on its specified finite-Tor domains; field coefficients use scalar localization and common finite fields, never a reduction from a field to $A_{E,n}$. Weil-equivariance is the statement for objects equipped with the Weil data of the cited coefficient theorem.

source.place: Proof, clause (7): coefficient and Weil coherence
